analyzed_vuln.description: `ArrayData::GetNullCount()` computes nulls by calling `CountSetBits(this->buffers[0]->data(), this->offset, this->length)` without validating that the null bitmap buffer is large enough for `offset + length` bits. With malformed IPC input, an array can be constructed whose validity bitmap is undersized relative to its declared length/offset. During `ValidateArray()` the call to `array.null_count()` triggers `GetNullCount()`, which then causes `CountSetBits()` to read past the end of the bitmap (crash at bit_util.cc:95 in the popcount loop).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `arrow-ipc-stream-fuzz`, attacker-controlled IPC stream data is decoded into arrays/record batches. The PoV creates inconsistent array metadata (notably length/offset vs validity bitmap size), especially through nested list validation paths. `RecordBatch::ValidateFull()` -> `ValidateArray()` calls `array.null_count()`, which reaches `ArrayData::GetNullCount()`. If `null_count` is unknown and `buffers[0]` exists but is too small, `CountSetBits` performs out-of-bounds reads, producing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
